fields.title: A manual is a symptom, not a solution
fields.keyTakeaway: Every manual written should start as an attempt to eliminate the need for it. If it cannot be eliminated, the manual is written for a specific task and lives right where the user gets stuck, not in a separate document.
fields.checkQuestion: Store clerks don't understand how to cancel an erroneous scan. What is your first move?
fields.blocks/0/text: The key question of this node: **how to use the product to solve tasks?** The question sounds like "write documentation", but starts earlier.
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer this question.** Support answers the exact same question twenty times a month. They write a guide, nobody reads it, the volume of questions remains unchanged.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: A manual is the last step, not the first
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **1. Eliminate.** Can we make it so the question never arises? Often this is a one-hour fix.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **2. Guide at the friction point.** If you can't eliminate it—provide a quick hint right where the user pauses, not in a "Help" section.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **3. Write.** If even that is impossible—write concise text for a specific task: "how to cancel an erroneous scan", not a general "user manual".
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Verification:** volume of support tickets on this topic. If it hasn't dropped, you merely wrote documentation instead of solving the problem.
fields.blocks/3/text:
The question was always the same: "scanned the wrong item, how do I remove it". The app had a cancel function—a long press on the row.

The first instinct: write a manual. Instead, they added a cancel button directly to the row of the last scanned item. Three hours of work.

Support tickets dropped to two a month—from users wanting to remove an earlier item rather than the last one. For that case, they wrote four lines of text right on the list screen.
fields.blocks/3/title: Polka, twenty support tickets a month
fields.blocks/4/text: People look for answers at the moment of friction and on the screen where they got stuck. A document residing separately from that context is read only by those paid to read it.
fields.blocks/4/title: Almost nobody reads the user manual
fields.blocks/5/text: There are domains where documentation is mandatory and non-negotiable: safety regulations, legally binding actions, pre-onboarding training. There, the goal is not to eliminate text, but to ensure it is precise.
